hunks.sol: As the hour of the Rooster began, an old beggar watched the sun inch toward the western mountains and muttered to himself.

hunks.baseline: The other beggars huddled around a nearby campfire reacted to his words.
hunks.sol: The other beggars huddled around a nearby campfire looked up.

hunks.baseline: “Then what about weather like this at this time of year? Does that make sense?”
hunks.sol: “Does weather like this make sense at this time of year?”

hunks.baseline: “Right. It’s not like this just started yesterday or the day before.”

hunks.baseline: He had a point.

hunks.sol: They had a point. The world hadn’t gone haywire just yesterday.

hunks.baseline: The old beggar—or rather, Man Chong, Branch Master of the Beggars’ Sect’s Xining branch in Qinghai—let out a small sigh and walked toward the fire.
hunks.sol: The old beggar—Man Chong, Branch Master of the Beggars’ Sect’s Xining branch in Qinghai—sighed and walked toward the fire.

hunks.baseline: “Why, of course. Even if we don’t have a damn thing, we’re the sort who’ll find a way to fill our bellies.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. We may not have a damn thing to our names, but we always find a way to fill our bellies.”

hunks.baseline: “You saved some for the ones out on patrol, didn’t you?”
hunks.sol: “You saved some for the ones out on patrol?”

hunks.baseline: “Come now. Do you take us for beggars with no sense of decency? Don’t worry. There’s enough for them to come back and eat their fill, too.”
hunks.sol: “Come now. Do you take us for beggars with no decency? Don’t worry. There’s enough for them to come back and eat till they burst.”

hunks.baseline: One of the beggars grinned, yellow teeth showing, and offered him a steaming bowl. Man Chong found himself smacking his lips.
hunks.sol: One of the beggars grinned, showing his yellow teeth, and held out a steaming bowl. Man Chong found his mouth watering.

hunks.baseline: “Just eat it. You’ll see it tastes just as good as it smells.”
hunks.sol: “Just eat it. You’ll see it tastes as good as it smells.”

hunks.baseline: Man Chong polished off the bowl in the blink of an eye, then patted his full belly with a satisfied smile.
hunks.sol: Man Chong emptied the bowl in no time, then patted his full belly with a satisfied smile.

hunks.baseline: It looked like a hodgepodge of the highest order, but perhaps because it had been made with fish freshly caught in Qinghai Lake, it tasted as if it had come from a first-rate chef.
hunks.sol: It looked like a hodgepodge if ever there was one, but perhaps because it was made with fish freshly caught in Qinghai Lake, it tasted like the work of a first-rate chef.

hunks.baseline: As he watched the waters of Qinghai Lake slowly bathe in the sunset, he felt his worries wash away, if only for a moment.
hunks.sol: As he watched the waters of Qinghai Lake slowly take on the colors of the sunset, he felt his worries wash away, if only for a moment.

hunks.baseline: Of course, the reality was still bleak.
hunks.sol: Reality, of course, was still bleak.

hunks.baseline: The situation had hardly improved, even after Jin Taekyung and the reinforcements passed through here and joined the others in Xining about four days ago.
hunks.sol: The situation had hardly improved since Jin Taekyung and the reinforcements passed through here to join the others in Xining about four days ago.

hunks.baseline: No—the situation was getting worse by the day, as if to crush that brief glimmer of hope.
hunks.sol: No—it was getting worse by the day, as if to crush that brief glimmer of hope.

hunks.baseline: *At this rate, we’ll be surrounded from both sides for sure… Damn it. We’re caught in a hell of a mess.*
hunks.sol: *At this rate, we’ll be surrounded from both sides… Damn it. We’re caught in a hell of a mess.*

hunks.baseline: The mere thought of Dark Heaven’s massive army, which had already taken Kunlun Mountain, was enough to send a chill down his spine. And from the rear, bandits who’d dealt the Central Plains Murim a vicious blow were said to be swarming in like ants.
hunks.sol: The mere thought of Dark Heaven’s massive army occupying Kunlun Mountain sent a chill down his spine. And from the rear, bandits who’d dealt the Central Plains Murim a vicious blow were said to be swarming in like ants.

hunks.baseline: There was only one thing they had going for them.

hunks.sol: The fullness in his belly vanished. Anxiety and fear took its place.

hunks.baseline: “……Damn it.”
hunks.sol: “…Damn it.”

hunks.sol: His mood souring in an instant, Man Chong snatched up a pebble within reach and hurled it.

hunks.baseline: Whoosh!
hunks.sol: *Whoosh!*

hunks.baseline: His clothes were shabby, but he was a master of the Beggars’ Sect with years of experience behind him.
hunks.sol: His clothes were shabby, but he was a seasoned Branch Master and a master of the Beggars’ Sect.

hunks.baseline: Splash!
hunks.sol: *Splash!*

hunks.baseline: He stopped when he saw the ripples from the pebble settle and the water slowly return to stillness.
hunks.sol: He stopped when the ripples from the pebble settled and the water slowly grew still again.

hunks.baseline: It didn’t take long for him to understand the sudden sense of déjà vu.
hunks.sol: It didn’t take him long to place the sudden sense of déjà vu.

hunks.baseline: No—it was as black as if someone had poured ink into it.
hunks.sol: No—as black as if someone had poured ink into it.

hunks.baseline: The waters of Qinghai Lake, which had been tinted with sunset only moments ago, were no longer beautiful. Even the quiet conversations reaching his ears felt unusually ominous.
hunks.sol: Only moments ago, the waters of Qinghai Lake had glowed with the sunset. Now there was nothing beautiful about them, and even the quiet conversation behind him sounded strangely ominous.

hunks.baseline: “Man, why’s it getting dark so fast today? Usually it takes half an hour for the sun to set.”
hunks.sol: “Man, why’s it getting dark so fast today? Usually the sunset alone lasts half an hour.”

hunks.baseline: “I certainly won’t say no. Oh, Branch Master, would you like another bowl?”
hunks.sol: “Don’t mind if I do. Branch Master, would you like another bowl?”

hunks.baseline: More precisely, he couldn’t.
At that moment, his instincts were sounding a red alarm in his head.
hunks.sol: He couldn’t. Every instinct he had was sounding an alarm.

hunks.baseline: Of course, it could be nothing, just as the other Beggars’ Sect disciples seemed to think.
hunks.sol: Of course, it could be nothing, as the other Beggars’ Sect disciples seemed to think.

hunks.baseline: Frost had fallen before harvest season, and giant monsters with appearances that barely seemed human were running wild. What was left to be surprised by?
hunks.sol: Frost had fallen before harvest season, and giant monsters that barely looked human were running wild. What was left to be surprised by?

hunks.baseline: But he had a feeling he couldn’t explain.
The experience he’d built up in more than sixty years, the instinct of an old master etched into his bones.
hunks.sol: But he had a feeling he couldn’t explain. More than sixty years of experience—and an old veteran’s instinct, etched into his bones.

hunks.sol: “The patrol. When are they due back?”

hunks.sol: The old Branch Master was usually so easygoing that his sudden bark left the disciples stammering.

hunks.sol: “W-well, they’re about half a gak later than usual, but they must be close by now. There’s no need to worry, Branch Master… Huh?”

hunks.sol: One of the disciples trailed off, eyes widening as he looked over Man Chong’s shoulder. Everyone turned.

hunks.sol: On a low hill about two hundred zhang away, a group of men and horses had just appeared, tiny as specks. They were slowly descending through the gathering darkness.

hunks.baseline: “Speak of the devil. They’re right on time.”
hunks.sol: “Speak of the devil. There they are.”

hunks.baseline: “Branch Master, you can relax. I’ll give them a proper scolding this time.”
hunks.sol: “Branch Master, you can settle down. I’ll give them a proper scolding.”

hunks.sol: As the others offered excuses while watching his expression, Man Chong stared at the patrol and murmured, almost like a groan.

hunks.baseline: “Twelve. Unless my eyes are wrong.”
hunks.sol: “Twelve. Unless my eyes are playing tricks on me.”

hunks.baseline: Someone began to ask, then suddenly faltered.
hunks.sol: The disciple’s question died on his lips.

hunks.baseline: The patrol that had left about two shichen ago to survey the area had numbered ten.
hunks.sol: The patrol that had left to survey the area about two shichen ago had numbered ten.

hunks.baseline: “Could be one of two things. Either they found survivors who made it through by sheer luck…”
hunks.sol: “One of two things. Either they found survivors who escaped by sheer luck…”

hunks.baseline: “Get to the boat now. We’ll raise anchor, put some distance between us, then see what happens.”
hunks.sol: “Get to the boat. Raise anchor, put some distance between us, and then we’ll see what they do.”

hunks.baseline: “W-we’ll do as you say!”
hunks.sol: “Y-yes, Branch Master!”

hunks.baseline: The disciples finally realized how serious the situation was and moved into action without another word.
hunks.sol: At last grasping the danger, the disciples moved as one.

hunks.sol: By the time they’d boarded the boat moored by the shore and rowed a safe distance away, the unidentified group had reached the campfire they’d left behind.

hunks.baseline: Man Chong’s sudden shout was answered from beyond the darkness, which had grown noticeably deeper.
hunks.sol: An answer came from beyond the darkness, which had grown noticeably deeper.

hunks.sol: Man Chong’s face went rigid.

hunks.sol: Worse, the voice from the darkness sounded exactly like Seok Sam’s.

hunks.baseline: Leaving the Beggars’ Sect disciples behind, their faces pale as if they’d seen a ghost, Man Chong gritted his teeth and shouted again.
hunks.sol: Leaving the pale-faced disciples behind him, Man Chong gritted his teeth and shouted again.

hunks.baseline: A brief silence followed.
It lasted only a moment, but felt longer than ever—like an eternity.
hunks.sol: Silence followed. It lasted only a moment, yet felt longer than any silence he’d ever known.

hunks.baseline: Then an unfamiliar voice suddenly rang out, shattering the silence that seemed ready to suffocate them.
hunks.sol: Then an unfamiliar voice shattered it.

hunks.baseline: With a buoyant voice that even carried a hint of laughter, the figure that had only been a silhouette emerged into view, heading for the still-burning campfire.
hunks.sol: There was even a hint of laughter in the man’s buoyant voice. A shape that had been nothing but a silhouette emerged into the light of the still-burning campfire.

hunks.baseline: Tap-tap.
hunks.sol: *Tap-tap.*

hunks.baseline: Between the sparks rising into the air, a man and a horse crossed the gravel without a sound. Man Chong’s eyes widened at the sight.
hunks.sol: Amid the sparks rising into the air, a man and horse crossed the gravel without the slightest sound. Man Chong’s eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: For a moment, he was speechless.
hunks.sol: For a moment, he couldn’t speak.

hunks.baseline: Partly because of the skeletal horse, its white bones exposed, but more than that, because the man sitting casually atop it filled him with a fear he’d never experienced before.
hunks.sol: The horse was a skeleton, its white bones exposed. But it was the man seated so casually on its back who filled him with a fear unlike anything he’d ever known.

hunks.baseline: Grin.
He showed his unnaturally white teeth—sharp fangs like a wild beast’s.
hunks.sol: The man grinned, baring unnaturally white teeth and fangs as sharp as a wild beast’s.

hunks.baseline: And those blood-red eyes, gleaming clearly even from far away, seemed to bind his body and mind just by meeting his gaze.
hunks.sol: His blood-red eyes gleamed even at this distance. Just meeting his gaze felt as though it bound Man Chong’s body and mind.

hunks.baseline: The man shrugged at Man Chong, whose body was trembling.
hunks.sol: The man shrugged at the trembling Man Chong.

hunks.baseline: His nonchalant manner only made him more terrifying. But Man Chong managed to force out his voice.
hunks.sol: His nonchalance only made him more terrifying. Man Chong forced out a question.

hunks.baseline: “Aw. How touching. Guess you’ve grown pretty attached to them begging for a living?”
hunks.sol: “Aw. How touching. All that begging together must have made you close.”

hunks.baseline: “You bastard! Answer the question!”
hunks.sol: “You bastard! Answer me!”

hunks.baseline: “I mean, it’s hard to talk properly when a beggar’s yelling at you. Fine, fine. Don’t get so worked up.”
hunks.sol: “How am I supposed to talk with a beggar yelling at me? Fine, fine. Don’t get so worked up.”

hunks.baseline: The man waved a hand as if to calm him down, then smacked his lips.
hunks.sol: The man waved a hand as though calming him down, then smacked his lips.

hunks.baseline: “To sum it up, they went to a better place. Though they didn’t taste like much.”
hunks.sol: “To sum it up, they’ve gone to a better place. Didn’t taste like much, though.”

hunks.baseline: Man Chong froze, his mind settling on a suspicion too horrible to put into words. The man frowned.
hunks.sol: Man Chong froze at a thought too horrible to put into words. The man frowned.

hunks.baseline: “Hey, don’t get the wrong idea. Maybe it’s because they were mangy beggar bastards, but their bodies weren’t much to write home about either. I only drank a little blood, just to have some fun.”
hunks.sol: “Hey, don’t get the wrong idea. They were mangy beggar bastards, and their bodies weren’t much good either. I only drank a little blood to have some fun.”

hunks.baseline: “What? Not what you expected? That voice was pretty convincing, though.”
hunks.sol: “What? Was that not good enough for you? I thought I got the voice pretty close.”

hunks.baseline: Grit.
hunks.sol: *Grit.*

hunks.baseline: The taste of blood flooded Man Chong’s mouth.
hunks.sol: The taste of blood filled Man Chong’s mouth. Still, he clenched his teeth harder.

hunks.baseline: Even so, he gritted his teeth with all his strength.
It wasn’t only the rage of losing a subordinate who’d been like a brother to him.

hunks.sol: It wasn’t only rage at losing a subordinate who had been like a brother to him. He had to do this—had to hold on somehow—to bear the fear tightening its grip on him with every passing moment.

hunks.baseline: The words had never seemed so chilling.

hunks.sol: Never had those words felt so chilling. Never had someone a hundred zhang away made him feel as though his head might come off at any moment.

hunks.baseline: The man—or rather, the Blood Lord—looked at Man Chong with a smile.
hunks.sol: The man—the Blood Lord—smiled at Man Chong.

hunks.baseline: Then he slowly scanned the twenty Beggars’ Sect disciples, frozen like statues around him, unable to react. Suddenly, he spoke.
hunks.sol: Then he slowly swept his gaze over the twenty Beggars’ Sect disciples, frozen like statues around him, and spoke.

hunks.baseline: “I’m planning to let at least one of you live. You’ll be glad one of you survived, and I need someone to deliver a message. Seems like a good deal for both of us, doesn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “I’m planning to let at least one of you live. One of you gets to survive, and I get someone to deliver a message. Good for both sides, isn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: “Quite a sight, those faces. What, did you think you could just run away?”
hunks.sol: “Look at your faces. What, did you think you could just run away?”

hunks.baseline: Grinning at their rigid faces a hundred zhang away, the Blood Lord suddenly turned around.
hunks.sol: The Blood Lord grinned at their rigid faces a hundred zhang away, then turned to look behind him.

hunks.baseline: “Time to get moving, isn’t it? It’s something we have to do anyway.”
hunks.sol: “Time to get moving, don’t you think? You have to do it anyway.”

hunks.sol: At his words, one of the figures waiting in the darkness stepped forward.

hunks.sol: Long robes brushed the gravel. As if the Blood Lord weren’t worth answering, the Grand Mage passed him, reached the lakeshore, and extended her hand.

*Crack-crack-crack!*

hunks.baseline: Faced with that unbelievable reality, they could do nothing.
hunks.sol: Faced with that impossible sight, they could do nothing.

hunks.baseline: Not even when the foul stench of monsters began to drift toward them from beyond the thick darkness in the distance.
hunks.sol: Not when the foul stench of monsters began to drift toward them from beyond the thick darkness.
